label: caiso 130 nameplate aware
definition: (KEEPER) caiso-130 single delta on the caiso-126 RoR-split keeper: hydro_budget_nameplate_aware. Applies the monthly hydro LEVEL target by water-filling under each plant-month's own EIA-860 nameplate x hours ceiling, re-allocating the overflow to the plant-months that can still deliver it, instead of a uniform fleet-wide monthly scale factor whose excess the LP silently clipped (P[g,t] <= pmax x availability). Closes the FINDING-caiso126 K4 defect: 130.2/352.7/26.3 GWh re-allocated over 70/52/27 clipped plant-months, 0 GWh physically unattainable, 0 MWh left above the bound. Zero new free parameters -- the bound is the plant's own nameplate and the calendar. Promoted on rule 1/14 structural grounds over a regressed overnight window gate (K2-2024, overnight gap 92 -> 152 MW): the rubric is identical to the same-HEAD control, and the uniform scale's silent clip was compensating for the model's own overnight hydro excess, so reverting would bury the error inside an inaccurate input.
market_story: Conventional hydro: a plant cannot generate above its nameplate, so a monthly energy budget that exceeds nameplate x hours-in-month is water the plant can never put on the grid. CAISO's measured monthly hydro level (EIA-930 NG: WAT) is real and the fleet does deliver it; what was wrong was the model's allocation of that level across plants -- a uniform fleet-wide scale inflated small plants past their physical ceiling and the LP quietly dropped the difference, so the modeled fleet under-delivered its own measured water by 0.13-0.35 TWh/yr. Water-filling under each plant's nameplate puts that energy on the plants that can actually pass it, which is what the real fleet does: operators route inflow to the units with capacity left. Hydro (annual mean MW): the fleet now delivers 98/96/93 % of the re-allocated water, +14.5/+37.5/+2.8 MW closer to measured in 2023/24/25. Belly (h9-15): improves every year (-92 -> -79, -58 -> -27, -83 -> -81 MW) as the freed water serves the solar-belly shoulder the pure-economic budget had been leaving to gas. Overnight (h0-6): worsens (+160 -> +177, +92 -> +152, +211 -> +214 MW) -- a plurality of the freed water lands here rather than in the evening, because the receiving plant-months are the ones with nameplate headroom left, and their headroom sits in the hours they were not already running flat out. That is an exposed defect, not a bought residual: the model's evening-overnight premium is compressed ~2x by its own storage arbitrage (caiso-127), so the LP's lambda surface does not reward concentrating water in the evening peak. Gas: falls 0.08/0.27/0.02 TWh as hydro displaces it, which widens the standing C5a CO2 deficit -- a real cost of this delta, second-order against a 6-8 TWh gap.
